meta.title: Session Pilot
meta.subtitle: Your sessions, limits and tokens, inside Claude Code
meta.author: Hans Tandt

blocks.text: How to use this manual
Chapters 1 to 12 are for everyone who uses Claude Code. The appendix is for developers: how the mod works and how to check it.

blocks.title: Unofficial project
blocks.text: Session Pilot (formerly the AI Usage Meter mod) is an unofficial community project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Anthropic. "Claude" is a trademark of Anthropic.
1. See your limits inside Claude Code

The mod shows your Claude usage in a band just above the prompt, where you type. Claude Code makes room for it, so it never covers your work. It works in the desktop app's Code tab and in the terminal.

blocks.caption: Figure 1. The band above the prompt. At yellow and red it tells you what to do next, with a button.
blocks.alt: Three bands with Session, Week and Compress: green at 46 %, yellow at 84 % with a Write session notes button, red at 93 % with Write session notes and Compact.

rows: Your 5-hour limit: how much is used, and the time until it resets.
Your weekly limit, the same way.
How full this conversation is. When it is full, Claude Code shrinks it to a short summary (compaction) and details get lost, so save your notes before that.
About how many more messages, with Claude's answers, fit before compaction, if they are as long as the last few.
At your pace so far you reach the limit before it resets.
The figures are old. Claude Code sends new ones with its next reply.
How long the conversation stays cheap to continue: 42 minutes left (chapter 11).
With the Haiku reader on: the part of this session's work done by the cheaper Haiku (chapter 6).
Only if you set a token number in the Settings: the conversation passed it (chapter 11).
Another Claude Code session on this PC is at red.

blocks.title: The little robot
blocks.text: It shows at a glance what Claude is doing. It blinks now and then, its eyes move while Claude works, and its antenna has the Compress colour (green, orange or red). It also shows which model is answering, because some cost far more than others: Opus, the strongest and most expensive, wears a crown; Sonnet has ears; Haiku, the cheapest, has a short antenna; Fable has two antenna points. The five marks under it show the effort: how hard Claude thinks before it answers, from low (1 mark) to max (5). More effort helps with difficult work, but uses more of your limits. When Close session says it is safe to close, the robot cheers. In the terminal it is a short face, such as {o_o} for Haiku. Size and options are in the Settings (chapter 7).

blocks.title: The band is gone and you see [+]
blocks.text: Claude Code itself folded it: a click on its `[-]` mark at the right end of the band, or `ctrl+x ctrl+a`. Click `[+]` or press `ctrl+x ctrl+a` again to get the band back. The mod cannot fold or unfold it.

blocks.title: Other languages
blocks.text: Under Settings, Language switches the screens to Nederlands, Français or Deutsch. Button labels and the names Session, Week and Compress stay in English in every language.
2. Why it helps

Claude remembers only what fits in its context window: everything Claude keeps in mind during one session. When the window is full, Claude Code compacts it. The older part of the conversation becomes a short summary, and the details are gone. Claude goes on, but may forget paths, rules and decisions.

The mod warns you before that happens, so you can write down what matters and start a fresh session. It also shows how much of your 5-hour and weekly limits is left, so a limit never stops you by surprise.
3. Install it
The mod is a folder. Put it somewhere it can stay, for example `Documents\Session Pilot`: Claude Code reads the mod from that folder, so do not move or delete it later.

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: Claude Code 2.1.287 or later, and a Claude plan with usage limits (Pro or Max). Older versions do not know the install command below and cannot show the band, so update first (step 3).

items: Unzip the mod into that folder.
Open PowerShell.
Update Claude Code first: type `claude update`, then `claude --version`. It must show 2.1.287 or later. Still an older version? Close PowerShell, open a new one and check again.
Type the command below, with your own folder between the quotes, and press Enter.
Quit and restart the Claude desktop app, or start a new `claude` session in the terminal.
Send one message. After Claude's reply, the band appears above the prompt.

blocks.text: One command adds the mod and installs it for every session:

blocks.title: "error: unknown option '--marketplace'"
blocks.text: Your `claude` is older than 2.1.287, or PowerShell still uses the old one. Update it and open a new PowerShell. Cannot update? Install with two commands instead: `claude plugin marketplace add "C:\Users\<you>\Documents\Session Pilot"`, then `claude plugin install ai-usage-meter@ai-usage-meter`. The band itself still needs 2.1.287 or later.

blocks.title: Coming from the AI Usage Meter mod?
blocks.text: Session Pilot is the same mod with a new name: your settings stay. Unzip the new version, copy everything inside its Session Pilot folder over your old AI Usage Meter Mod folder (replace the files), and restart Claude Code. Keep the old folder where it is: Claude Code reads the mod from there.

blocks.title: Try it for one session first
blocks.text: In a terminal, type `claude --plugin-dir "C:\Users\<you>\Documents\Session Pilot"`. The mod then loads for that session only, and nothing is installed.

blocks.title: "Detected a custom API key"
blocks.text: If Windows has an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` variable, Claude Code asks whether to use it. Choose No: with an API key, Claude Code reports no 5-hour or weekly limits, so Session and Week stay empty, and every message is billed per token.
Without the terminal
No `claude` command in your terminal? Then tell Claude Code where the folder is, in `settings.json`:

items: Open `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json` in a text editor.
Find `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` in the `env` block. If it is not there, add it.
Add the mod's folder to its value. Separate folders with a semicolon (`;`).
Save the file and restart Claude Code.

blocks.caption: The env block with the strip's add-on and the mod. In JSON every \ is written twice.

blocks.text: 4. Write your session notes in time

items: At yellow (80 %), a second line appears: finish the task and update your session notes.
Click Write session notes. Claude writes down what was done, the decisions, what is still open and the next steps.
At red (90 %), the line says start a new session. Start one, and let it read the notes. It blinks until the context drops back.

blocks.text: At red the status line under the prompt says the same, so you see it even with the band hidden.

blocks.title: A new session beats Compact
blocks.text: At red the band also offers Compact. Compaction keeps only a summary of the older conversation, not the details. When you can, write the notes and start a new session instead.
5. Close and start a session safely

Two buttons run two prompts that come with the mod. Close session checks everything this session did and saves it in CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md and the session notes. Start session reads those files in the next session, or creates them in a new project, and continues where you stopped. Run Close session again later in the same session, and it updates the note it already wrote instead of adding a second one: the open steps stay word for word, and older notes are never shortened.

rows: In the band at red, in the /meter pane, or `/meter close-session`.
In the band of a new session before your first message, in the /meter pane, or `/meter start`.

blocks.title: In the desktop app: type /meter start
blocks.text: In the desktop app, the band of a new session only appears after your first message. So don't type a question first: type /meter start as your very first message and press Enter. That does the same as the Start session button: Claude gets only the Start session prompt and doesn't start on anything else.

blocks.caption: Figure 2. Close session in the band: first its progress, then the result.
blocks.alt: Two bands: an orange line "Closing session… step 3 of 6 · 50%" with a bar, and a green line "Now it's safe to end this session".

rows: Wait: Claude is working through the check.
✓ Now it's safe to end this session
Everything is saved. Close the session.
✓ Everything is ready to start this session
Claude has read the files. Start your task.
It's NOT safe to close this session: <reason>
Claude found a problem. Read its reply, fix it, and run Close session again.
Close session stopped at step 2 of 6
The reply ended early. Check it, or run Close session again.

blocks.title: One click does it all
blocks.text: The button counts as your "go": Claude writes the changes without stopping to ask. In a git project it makes no backup copies of files that git already keeps.

blocks.title: The hand-over
blocks.text: Close session ends with the first message for the next session. The mod keeps it, and Start session in the next session of the same folder sends it along. Claude continues exactly where you stopped.
6. Open the details

blocks.caption: Figure 3. /meter shows both limits, this session's context, the last turns and your other sessions.
blocks.alt: The details pane: the Session and Week bars with reset times, the Compress bar at 84 %, a small chart of the last turns, three buttons and two other sessions.

rows: Open the details pane. Or click Details in the band; click it again to close the pane.
Switch the band, the pane and the messages to Dutch (en, nl, fr or de).
Hide the band. `/meter band on` shows it again.

blocks.text: Short messages (toasts) appear at each warning level, when a limit resets and when compaction has run. A limit warning shows once, even with several sessions open.

blocks.title: The Haiku reader (off by default)
blocks.text: Most of Claude's work is reading files, and reading with Opus, the expensive model, adds up fast. With the reader on (On in the pane), the mod watches how much Opus reads for one answer. Above a limit (2,000 tokens, a few pages), it suggests that Opus lets a reader on the cheaper Haiku do the rest of the searching and reading. The reader sends back only where the answer is: the file, the line numbers and those exact lines. Opus reads those lines itself, and always reads a file itself before it changes it. The pane shows how much of this session's work Haiku did ("Haiku 19 %") and how often the reader ran; Details shows the tokens per model for this session and this week.
See the warnings with demo figures

rows: This session at 85 % of compaction: the yellow warning.
A demo session called demo-A at 93 %, shown as another session.

blocks.text: In the terminal the mod works the same. The bars are drawn as lines, and `/meter` opens the pane beside the conversation in the fullscreen layout (`/tui fullscreen`, at least 110 columns), or above the prompt.
7. Change the settings

Open the /meter pane (click Details in the band) and click Settings at the bottom, or type /meter settings. Every setting has its own button: click On or Off to switch it, − or + to change a number, and a choice (such as the Haiku reader) to go to the next option. A change applies at once. Only the colours can't be changed there: open a terminal, type claude, then /config, and look for the ai-usage-meter rows. In the desktop app, /config opens the app's own Settings window, which doesn't have the mod's settings. The first setting, Language, sets the language of the band, the pane and the short messages: English, Nederlands, Français or Deutsch (or type /meter language nl). Button labels and the names Session, Week and Compress stay in English.

rows: Robot: a different robot for each model
Haiku reader: from (tokens read in one turn)
Colours: below the warnings, first, second
Use the strip's Settings when it is installed

blocks.title: Which settings are used?
blocks.text: When the AI Usage Meter strip is installed, the bottom of the /meter pane says "The AI Usage Meter strip's Settings decide them" (chapter 8). Otherwise the mod's own settings apply.
8. Use it with the AI Usage Meter strip
The AI Usage Meter strip is a separate Windows program: a small bar that stays on top of your other windows. The mod and the strip work together.

items: Both write the same figures to the same files, so each shows every session on this PC.

With the strip installed, the mod uses the strip's Settings window for levels, colours and messages. Switch off Use the strip's Settings when it is installed in the Settings (chapter 7) to use the mod's own settings.
The mod is called ai-usage-meter and the strip's add-on usage-meter. They run side by side; the strip's demo stays /usage-demo.

blocks.text: 9. Check that everything works
Ten minutes, no usage spent on the warnings: the demo figures show every colour and button. Use a test folder, not a real project. Do the steps in this order.

blocks.text: 10. Remove it

items: Type `claude plugin uninstall ai-usage-meter@ai-usage-meter`.
Type `claude plugin marketplace remove ai-usage-meter`.
Restart Claude Code. Now you can delete the mod's folder.

blocks.text: Installed through `settings.json`? Then remove the folder, and the semicolon before it, from `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` instead. The mod's figures stay in `%USERPROFILE%\.claude` for the strip; session files older than 7 days are deleted.
11. Save tokens: how Claude uses them

Every Claude plan has two limits: one for 5 hours and one for the week. They fill up with tokens. A token is a small piece of text, a bit less than a word; one page of text is a few hundred tokens. Everything Claude reads and writes costs tokens. This chapter explains in plain words where they go, and what the mod's four tools do to save them. You don't need any of them: three of the four are off until you switch them on.
Where the tokens go

items: Claude rereads the whole conversation for every message. It doesn't remember anything between two messages: each time you send one, it reads everything again from the start, your messages, its answers and every file it opened. So the longer the conversation, the more each new message costs. When the conversation gets too long, Claude Code replaces it with a short summary (compaction). That makes room, but details get lost; that is why the mod warns you to save your notes first.

Rereading is cheaper when the conversation was used recently. Claude Code keeps a ready copy of the conversation for a while (the cache), like a book left open on your desk. A message within that time rereads from the ready copy, which costs much less. The copy stays ready for 1 hour after the last message on a Claude plan (5 minutes with an API key). After that the book goes back on the shelf: the next message rereads everything at the full price.
Opus is the strongest model and the most expensive one. Haiku is fast and much cheaper: good at finding and reading, less good at judging.

For a big search Claude can send out a helper. The helper searches on its own, and only its short answer comes back into your conversation. Your conversation doesn't grow with everything the helper read.

blocks.text: A warning at a number of tokens (off by default)

The band normally turns yellow at 80 % and red at 90 % of the point where compaction starts. In a very large conversation window (1 million tokens), 80 % only comes at about 775,000 tokens, while every message has been expensive for a long time. In the Settings (chapter 7) you can therefore also give a number of tokens, for example yellow from 250,000 and red from 350,000. The warning then comes at whichever is reached first, and says which, for example "262k tokens: finish the task and update your session notes". Leave it at 0 for a normal-sized window: then nothing changes.
The cache clock and Keep warm

After each reply, the band shows how long the ready copy of the conversation stays ready, for example "cache 42m": 42 minutes left. In the last 5 minutes it turns orange. After that it says "cache cold": your next message will cost the full price once, and then the copy is ready again.

Keep warm, a button in the /meter pane, sets that clock back to the start. It sends Claude one tiny hidden question ("reply with the word: ok"). To answer it, Claude rereads the conversation from the ready copy, and that keeps the copy ready for another full period. The question and its answer don't appear in your conversation: you only see a short message that it worked. Keep warm never runs by itself: one click is one question.

blocks.title: Example: a lunch break
blocks.text: You are in the middle of a long task and the band shows "cache 8m". You go to lunch for 45 minutes. Click Keep warm before you leave: the clock goes back to 60 minutes, and your first message after lunch still costs the low price. Without Keep warm, the copy would run out during lunch, and that first message would reread the whole conversation at the full price. Going home for the day? Then don't click it: you would pay for a question you never use.
Search helpers on Haiku (off by default)

When Claude has to search through many files, Claude Code sends out its search helper (called Explore). Normally that helper uses the same model as your conversation, often the expensive Opus. With "Search helpers (Explore) on Haiku" switched on in the Settings, it uses the cheaper Haiku instead. Searching and reading is what Haiku does well; Opus still does the thinking and makes the changes. Other helpers keep their model. Details next to the Haiku reader in the pane shows how many search helpers ran on Haiku.
Good to know

items: The mod can't tell you exactly how much you saved. It counts the tokens per model, but what the same work would have cost without these tools can only be guessed. To compare, look at the Session figure for the same kind of task, once with the tools on and once off.

Keep warm costs a little every time: Claude rereads the conversation from the ready copy. It is only worth it if you come back and carry on before the clock runs out. When the band already says "cache cold", Keep warm can't help, and the mod tells you so.
Haiku can miss details. Let it find and read, and let Opus check the result. Opus always reads a file itself before it changes it. For delicate work, switch the Haiku tools off.
The mod can't see how long the copy really stays ready: it uses the time set in the Settings (60 minutes). Set 5 minutes if you use an API key.
Every question the mod sends to a model (Keep warm, the reader's searches) counts toward your limits too.

blocks.title: A good start
blocks.text: Yellow from 250,000 tokens, red from 350,000, the cache clock on, the reader and search helpers off. Switch those on for days with a lot of searching, and watch the Haiku share in the pane.
12. HTML versions of your documents

A long Markdown document, such as a plan or a comparison, is hard to read as one long text. The mod can offer a readable HTML version: a web page with a table of contents and simple diagrams, which you open in your browser. It costs extra tokens, because Claude writes the whole document again with a layout, so the mod never makes one without your yes. The Markdown file stays the original: the HTML version is a reading copy next to it.
How it works

items: Claude writes a long Markdown document worth reading again: a plan, a specification, a comparison, a design or a process.
When Claude has finished, the band asks "An HTML version of Plan.md?" with Make it and No. The prompt box also shows the grey suggestion "Make the HTML version of Plan.md".
To say yes: click Make it, or press Tab and then Enter. Typing yes works too.
Claude writes Plan.html next to Plan.md. Double-click it in File Explorer to open it in your browser.
Changed the Markdown later? Then the mod offers to update the HTML version.

blocks.text: When it asks, and when not

items: Only for a long document (more than about one screen) that is also a plan, a specification, a comparison or similar, or that describes steps, a process or a timeline. In a folder where you said yes before, it asks a little sooner.
Never for CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, the session notes, change logs or task lists: those stay Markdown.
Once per document and session.
Sending another message instead, or clicking No, counts as "not now". After two in a row it stops asking for the rest of the session; /meter html ask turns the questions on again.
The diagrams are drawn inside the HTML file itself, so the page works without internet and you can send it to someone as one file.

blocks.text: Switch it

In the Settings of the /meter pane, HTML companion has three choices: ask (the default: the mod asks you), on (the mod makes the HTML version by itself, without asking) and off (never). You can also type /meter html ask, /meter html on or /meter html off. /meter html on its own makes the HTML version of the document on offer.

blocks.title: Only when you will read it again
blocks.text: Say yes for documents you will read again or share, such as a plan or a comparison. For a quick note, click No: the Markdown is enough, and you save the tokens.
Appendix: technical details
How it works

items: The mod is a Claude Code plugin with a hooks module (`hooks/register.tsx`). Claude Code runs it inside every session.
After each reply it reads the figures Claude Code reports: the 5-hour and weekly limits, the context fill and the cost. It measures the context against the auto-compaction point.
It draws the band and the /meter pane with Claude Code's own elements (`hooks/draw.tsx`): rounded bars on the desktop, lines in the terminal.
Every 30 seconds it reads the other sessions' files, so countdowns, old figures and other sessions stay up to date.
Every write is wrapped, so it can never break a Claude session.

blocks.text: What it reads and stores

rows: 5-hour and weekly percentages, reset times, time of the last update
Per session: folder name, fill, last activity, compaction time
Read only: the strip's settings, when the strip is installed
Whether the band is hidden, and which limit warnings were already shown

blocks.text: It reads no login or credentials and makes no network calls. The Write session notes button sends one ordinary message to Claude in your session, so it counts toward your limits like any message.
Check it
In the `MOD_Version` folder, `claude plugin validate .` checks the plugin the way Claude Code loads it, and `claude plugin test .` runs its tests on the terminal and desktop surfaces.
Limits

items: It sees Claude Code sessions on this PC only (app and terminal), not cloud or WSL sessions or other computers.
Session and Week need a Claude plan with usage limits; with an API key they stay empty.
Figures refresh when a session starts or replies. Chat use counts toward the limits but does not update them.
